{"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-23T14:00:47.842Z", "parent_tool_use_id": null, "uuid": "2219d3a1-f406-4a4d-8251-7cbea0b70afe", "session_id": "2d5b87f7-677d-4fe6-a443-9ae8ba2b8ded", "message": {"model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "id": "msg_011CgKHnGjap3ARh1LFpMZs6", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "tool_use", "id": "toolu_01BLVMgpXZJqJdz86w1LrnS4", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "mkdir -p .spektacular/tmp/20260101000000-jwt-auth && cd .spektacular/tmp/20260101000000-jwt-auth\ncat > changelog_project.md <<'E'\n# JWT authentication with integration docs\n\n## What was built\n\nStateless JWT authentication for the auth-service. A new `auth` package signs and verifies RS256 tokens and keeps a deny list of revoked token IDs. Three endpoints, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh` and `POST /auth/revoke`, use it: login returns an access token and a refresh token, refresh mints a new access token, and revoke blocks a token ID. In the docs repo, a new page `content/api/auth.md` describes all three endpoints with request and response shapes, and the API index links to it.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nReplaces session-based auth so the service can scale horizontally across backends. Any instance can validate tokens with only the public key. Integrators get a single reference for the new endpoints on day one.\n\n## Deviations from the plan\n\nNone.\nE\ncat > changelog_auth.md <<'E'\n# JWT authentication in the auth-service\n\nUsers can now log in and receive a signed access token plus a refresh token. They can exchange the refresh token for a new access token without sending credentials again, and revoke a token so it stops working. Requests with tampered or revoked tokens are rejected.\n\n> Derived from project auth-service (file), spec/plan 20260101000000-jwt-auth. See the project-level record for the full feature.\n\n## What changed in this repo\n\n- New `auth` package with RS256 signing, verification and a deny list (`auth/token.go`, `auth/denylist.go`, with tests).\n- Login, refresh and revoke handlers (`handlers/login.go`, `handlers/refresh.go`, `handlers/revoke.go`, with tests) wired up in `main.go`.\n\n## Why\n\nStateless tokens let every service instance validate requests independently, enabling horizontal scaling.\nE\ncat > changelog_docs.md <<'E'\n# JWT auth integration guide\n\nThe docs site now has an integration guide for the new authentication endpoints. It covers login, refresh and revoke, with the request and response shape of each, and is linked from the API index.\n\n> Derived from project auth-service (file), spec/plan 20260101000000-jwt-auth. See the project-level record for the full feature.\n\n## What changed in this repo\n\n- Added `content/api/auth.md` covering `/auth/login`, `/auth/refresh` and `/auth/revoke`.\n- Updated `content/api/index.md` to link to the new page.\n\n## Why\n\nIntegrators need a reference for the new endpoints before the feature is announced.\nE\ncd /app\nT=.spektacular/tmp/20260101000000-jwt-auth; P=20260101000000-jwt-auth\nspektacular changelog file write $P --from $T/changelog_project.md | head -c 300\nspektacular changelog file write $P --repo auth --from $T/changelog_auth.md | head -c 300\nspektacular changelog file write $P --repo docs --from $T/changelog_docs.md | head -c 300\nrm $T/changelog_*.md\nfind / -path /proc -prune -o -name '20260101000000-jwt-auth.md' -path '*changelog*' -print 2>/dev/null"}}]}}
